money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Cash declaration: French Customs requires anyone carrying cash, bearer negotiable instruments, prepaid cards or gold worth 10,000 euros or more (or the equivalent) to declare it, whether or not they live in France. 10,000 euros is about A$15,891 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = EUR 0.6293). Amounts of 50,000 euros or more also need proof of where the money came from. Declare online (the DALIA service, up to 30 days ahead) or on a paper form. Failing to declare can bring a fine of up to 50% of the amount and seizure of the cash. The page names Wallis and Futuna as an overseas collectivity, where Article L722-6 applies with its own dedicated form. The local currency is the CFP franc (XPF), issued through the Institut d'emission d'outre-mer. A French National Assembly report found by search (not reread in full) gives a fixed parity of 1,000 CFP francs = 8.38 euros.

items.text: Wallis and Futuna is an overseas collectivity of France. France's national drug penalties are: Using any narcotic, cannabis included, is banned even in private and for recreation. The usual response is a fixed fine of EUR 200 (about A$318 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293); a court can impose up to 1 year in prison and EUR 3,750 (about A$5,959). Service-Public's page is written for France as a whole; it does not say how each collectivity applies it.

Under Article 74 of the French Constitution each overseas collectivity has its own statute that sets out how national law applies there. Which parts of the drug-use rules apply here has not been confirmed from the statute.

facts.text: Wallis and Futuna is a French overseas collectivity and is not listed as its own WIPO member in the official IP-office directory. Official French IP law and INPI are the usual starting point, together with local official pages.

facts.label: Official IP office
facts.text: Patents, trademarks and related official registers start with Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), France.

facts.label: Ownership, licensing and filing
facts.text: Foreign ownership of IP, official licensing formalities, and whether the system is first-to-file, should be confirmed on the official IP office pages (and, where listed, on WIPO Lex). This pass records the official office rather than a full statute summary.
